classification.difficultyReason: Form a compound-interest equation with symbolic principal, cancel the principal and recover the annual rate using a square root.

content.prompt: Anthony invests $\$P$ for 2 years at $r\%$ p.a. compound interest. At the end of the 2 years, Anthony receives his original $\$P$ and $\dfrac{\$P}{10}$ in interest. Find $r$, correct to two decimal places.

answer.short:
$r\approx4.88$, so the annual interest rate is $4.88\%$.

The two-year growth factor is $1.1$; its positive square root gives the annual growth factor.
answer.worked:
The final amount is $P+\dfrac{P}{10}=\dfrac{11P}{10}$. Annual compounding gives
$$\begin{align*}P\left(1+\frac{r}{100}\right)^2&=\frac{11P}{10}\\\left(1+\frac{r}{100}\right)^2&=\frac{11}{10}\\1+\frac{r}{100}&=\sqrt{\frac{11}{10}}\\\frac{r}{100}&=\sqrt{\frac{11}{10}}-1\\r&=100\left(\sqrt{\frac{11}{10}}-1\right)\\r&\approx4.88.\end{align*}$$
The positive square root is used because the annual growth factor is positive. The annual interest rate is $4.88\%$.
